title: The Morning Brief: Wilson's record stands; FIFA fractures on World Cup plan
dek: Jacob Wilson set an MLB shortstop record with 111 consecutive errorless games as the Athletics beat Boston, while FIFA faces unified opposition from three continental confederations over Infantino's failed World Cup privatization scheme.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Wilson's defensive milestone marks a clean athletic achievement, while FIFA's governance crisis deepens as UEFA, Concacaf, and AFC formally accuse Infantino of breach of trust ahead of his March 2027 reelection.
bottom_line: Wilson's 111-game errorless streak is a clean athletic record that will stand until another shortstop surpasses it; FIFA's governance fracture is a structural crisis with Infantino facing formal accusations from three continental confederations a year before his reelection. The confederations' unified statement marks an unprecedented moment of aligned opposition. Watch whether Infantino resigns before March, whether other FIFA member associations align with the confederations' position, and whether preliminary confederation discussions about rival tournaments move to concrete structure.
body: Jacob Wilson's 111-game errorless streak at shortstop stands as the new MLB record, breaking Mike Bordick's 24-year-old mark of 110 games set in 2002. The 24-year-old Athletics shortstop last made an error on July 6 against San Francisco. The record came during Oakland's 4-3 victory over Boston at Fenway Park on Sunday, a win that ended the team's 12-game losing streak. Wilson handled five plays in that game: two popups, two grounders including a deep hit into the hole, and a double-play pivot.

On football's global stage, the FIFA governance crisis escalated sharply with three continental confederations issuing a formal joint accusation against president Gianni Infantino. UEFA, Concacaf, and the Asian Football Confederation released an open letter Monday calling Infantino's handling of the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal a "fundamental breach of trust" and "deception." The FFE plan would have created a new company to manage FIFA's commercial and tournament operations, with around 20 percent sold to private investors. FIFA stated last week it would not proceed with the proposal, and Infantino apologized to member associations over the development process. The confederations want Infantino to resign and are exploring preliminary discussions about organizing rival tournaments independent of FIFA.

LaLiga president Javier Tebas has separately declared the "Infantino era" over, stating the FIFA president's destructive management style extended well beyond the recent World Cup privatization dispute. Tebas told Le Monde he noticed the pattern years ago, though others are only recognizing it now. FIFA's own statement Saturday characterized the opposition as a "concerted and ongoing effort" to undermine the organization, asserting it does not identify specific entities behind the alleged coordinated campaign.

Elsewhere, Aaron McKenna won the IBF world middleweight title with a unanimous decision over previously unbeaten Etinosa Oliha in Dublin on August 9. Judges scored the 12-round bout 118-110, 117-111, and 116-112 in McKenna's favor. The 27-year-old from Monaghan extended his undefeated record to 21-0 in his first professional fight on Irish soil after nine years as a professional. Oliha fell to 22-1.

In tennis, World No. 1 Jannik Sinner withdrew from the Cincinnati Masters on August 9 due to a right knee injury. Sinner has not played since winning Wimbledon in July and said he is targeting the US Open, which begins August 30. His medical team is working to get him ready for that event.

In the NFL, the Carolina Panthers signed Kyle Trask as their third-string quarterback following a hamstring injury to undrafted rookie Haynes King during the Hall of Fame game in Canton. King had delivered a strong preseason debut, completing 21 of 34 passes for 180 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for the game-winning score in Carolina's 33-30 victory over Arizona on Thursday.

The New York Giants completed their first training camp under John Harbaugh at The Greenbrier in West Virginia, running 10 practices across 12 days. The defense emerged as a clear strength, with newly acquired linebackers Tremaine Edmunds and Arvell Reese both impressing in run defense. Reese, the No. 5 overall pick, "looked every bit the No. 5 pick," per ESPN. Both players "got their hands on passes all throughout" camp and made it difficult for offenses to complete passes over the middle. The offensive installation remains in progress, with quarterback Jaxson Dart still working to master the complex new scheme's under-center positioning.
